subject: Support renewal & latency SLO for KiteCloud
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@kitecloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Support renewal / latency SLO questions

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well — our current contract with Redwood comes up for renewal at the end of November and we want to tighten the latency guarantees for our primary inference path. Over the past year our traffic has doubled; we expect another 2.5x in the next 12 months.

Specifically we want to discuss:
- Moving to Premium Support (24x7, 30 min P1 response)
- A p95 latency SLO of 150ms for our /v1/generate route (current p95 is ~220ms)
- Dedicated capacity reservation for peak windows (estimate: 8 A100 equivalence) with an onramp over 8 weeks

Can you share a draft SLA and an order-of-magnitude price for a 12-month vs 24-month term? Also procurement will want an editable order form.

Attaching our usage snapshot separately — happy to jump on a call this week.

Thanks,
Alex Romero
Head of Platform
KiteCloud

Attachments: usage_snapshot_q3.csv (attachment stub)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@kitecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support renewal / latency SLO questions

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the usage snapshot, that helps.

Short answer: we can get you to p95 ~150ms with a combination of dedicated capacity + KV prefix caching and the Premium SLA. I’ve looped in Marcus (solutions) for sizing and Laura (account lead) for commercial options.

Proposed next steps:
1) Marcus to confirm sizing and suggest an 8-week onramp plan (staging -> warm -> full).
2) I’ll send a draft Premium SLA and an editable order form for procurement to review.
3) If you’re open, schedule a 30-minute technical + commercial call tomorrow or Thursday.

I’ve attached a working draft SLA and an order form for initial review — filenames below. We’ll mark up any latency measurement windows (p95 over 24h, exclusion windows for planned maintenance) per KiteCloud needs.

Olga Petrov
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: Redwood_Premium_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf (attachment stub); Order_Form_KC-1492_v2.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@kitecloud.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support renewal / latency SLO questions

Alex — quick technical note from my side:
- Based on your QPS spikes and model size, we recommend a dedicated pool equivalent to 7-9 A100s with 1.5x buffer for headroom.
- Enable prefix KV caching for the top 30% of frequent prefixes — that will reduce token compute by ~40% in our estimates and materially improve p95.
- We suggest a staged onramp: week 0-2 (capacity provisioning + smoke tests), week 3-5 (customer traffic samples + cache warm), week 6-8 (full cutover).

Operational guardrails I recommend including in the SLA:
- Defined maintenance windows and a single annual emergency maintenance exclusion
- Clear rollback policy and a canary route (5% traffic) for any model variant rollouts
- A runbook for incident classification (P1/P2/P3) with the 30-min P1 target you asked for

Happy to walk through these on a call.

—Marcus
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Romero <alex@kitecloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@kitecloud.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support renewal / latency SLO questions

Thanks Olga and Marcus — this looks promising. A couple of items from procurement and leadership:

1) Term: our CFO prefers a 12-month term but will consider 24 months if there’s an onboarding credit or step-down pricing in year 2.
2) Ramp credits: are you open to 20% credit on committed capacity for the first month of cutover while we validate traffic patterns?
3) Measurement: we need the p95 computed over rolling 24h and exposed in your Console with daily exportable reports for compliance.

Procurement has a couple of minor order form asks (tax fields, SAP vendor id). I’ve copied them on this thread.

Can we aim to finalize commercial terms by EOD Friday so we can hit a 1-Nov provisioning target?

Alex

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@kitecloud.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, procurement@kitecloud.com
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Support renewal / latency SLO questions

Alex / team — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Summary and commitments from Redwood: 

- Term & pricing: two options included in the attached order form — 12-month at list, 24-month with a 10% year-one effective discount and a step-down in year two.
- Onboarding credit: we will provide a one-month 20% committed capacity credit during the 8-week cutover window (applies to committed unit fees).
- SLA specifics: p95 latency measured over rolling 24h, reported in the Console with daily CSV exports. Emergency maintenance exclusion limited to 4 hours/year.
- Capacity & schedule: provision 8 A100-equivalent dedicated pool; staging in week 0-2, cache warm in week 3-5, full cutover by week 8.
- Docs & procurement: attached final SLA (Redwood_Premium_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf) and updated order form (Order_Form_KC-1492_v2.xlsx) — procurement fields populated where provided. DocuSign link below for signature.

Action items:
- Alex / procurement: confirm vendor details and which term you prefer by Monday 26 Oct.
- Laura: I’ll set up the DocuSign envelope and the kickoff call for Tue 2 Nov to align teams.

We’ll mark the deal KC-2026-1492 in HubSpot and flag the onboarding credit in billing. If you want any SLA clause tweaks I can have legal turn a redline in 24 hours.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
